web.title: Diya Spoon Relay: Diwali Kitty Party Game Rules and Twists
web.description: Diya Spoon Relay is a Diwali kitty party game where teams pass a diya spoon to spoon with no hands. How to play, rules, what you need, twists and FAQs.
web.intro: Diya Spoon Relay is a Diwali kitty party game where two teams pass a small LED or unlit clay diya down a line from spoon to spoon, with each lady holding a steel spoon in her mouth and her hands behind her back. The first team to get 5 diyas into its thali wins, but the last lady in the line must say a full Diwali wish to the host with the spoon still in her mouth before she can drop the diya. It needs only spoons, diyas, two bowls and two thalis, and takes about 10 minutes for 8 to 20 ladies.
materials: One clean steel spoon per lady (each uses her own)
10 LED tealight diyas or small unlit clay diyas (5 per team)
Two bowls to hold the diyas at the start
Two thalis or plates at the finish
steps: Split the group into two teams and stand each team in a straight line. Put a bowl of 5 diyas at the start of each line and an empty thali at the end.
Every lady holds a steel spoon in her mouth by the handle and keeps her hands behind her back. Only the first lady may use her hands, once, to place a diya on her spoon.
Pass the diya from spoon to spoon down the line without using hands. If it falls, it goes back to the start bowl.
The last lady walks to the host and says a full Diwali wish with the spoon still in her mouth, for example "Happy Diwali, didi!". Then she tips the diya into the thali and the next diya starts.
rules: Touching the diya or spoon with your hands sends the diya back to the start.
A dropped diya goes back to the start bowl.
If the wish is incomplete or she bursts out laughing, she must say it again.
The first team with all 5 diyas in its thali wins.
variations: Blindfold the last lady and let her team guide her to the host by voice.
Make every lady spin once on the spot before passing the diya.
The wish must include the host's name and the name of one Diwali sweet.
tips: Never use a lit diya or candle. LED tealights or empty clay diyas only.
Give every lady her own washed spoon so nobody shares.
Flat-bottomed diyas balance better than round ones, so start with those.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Diya Spoon Relay?
faq.a: At least 8 ladies, so each team has 4. It works up to 20, with 10 ladies per team.

faq.q: What do you need to play Diya Spoon Relay?
faq.a: One steel spoon per lady, 10 LED or unlit clay diyas, two bowls, two thalis and a timer. Everything is already in most homes during Diwali.

faq.q: Is it safe to use real diyas?
faq.a: Only unlit ones. Never pass a lit diya or candle. LED tealights look festive and are completely safe.

faq.q: Is Diya Spoon Relay good for a Diwali kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. It is quick, needs no prep, gets everyone laughing, and the Diwali wish twist makes it feel festive.

faq.q: How long does the game take?
faq.a: About 10 minutes for 5 diyas per team. Use 3 diyas per team if you are short on time.
